candidates.name: Existing signed KBD decision surface (KBD-METHOD prefix pattern) for KBD-POLICY-ACK
candidates.fit_for_gap: A: operator acknowledgement of a governing-policy conflict, bound to the policy file SHA-256, replaceable through --supersedes

evidence.claim: method-context.mjs:70-80 parses `KBD-METHOD <json>` decision summaries and drops superseded ones; the same loop can read `KBD-POLICY-ACK <json>`
`prometheus kbd decision record --id --summary --supersedes` exists; no new event kind or CLI command is needed
kbd-runtime Decision state is {id, summary, plan_revision, supersedes}; it carries no actor, so acknowledgement authority equals KBD-METHOD's existing trust model

risks: Authority is a decision recorded by whoever runs the CLI; the operator-label trust model is a deferred, pre-existing issue (#185-adjacent) and must be stated, not implied away
A hash-bound acknowledgement must be re-raised when the policy file changes; otherwise a stale ack silently covers new text
candidates.decision_rationale: Reuses the exact pattern already shipped for method selection; satisfies 'operator acknowledgement with provenance' without a new ledger, event or schema.

candidates.name: skills/process/kbd-process-orchestrator/references/method-context.md
candidates.fit_for_gap: B: single canonical text for the selected-method rules referenced by 11 stage skills

evidence.claim: All 11 stage SKILL.md sections already link references/method-context.md; the 13-line reference already holds the full rules
No test in scripts/tests or the orchestrator asserts on the copied section text

risks: A bare pointer may not be opened by a model; inline rules are followed more reliably. Mitigation: keep a short identical core (helper command, VLBV boundary, conflict surfacing) plus the pointer; POL-002 rerun measures it
Without a drift check the core can diverge again; add an equality check to an existing validator
candidates.decision_rationale: Adapt rather than build: shrink copies to an identical short core that points at the existing reference, and enforce identity with a check instead of inventing an include system.

candidates.name: scripts/tests/lib/kbd-194-196-sessions.mjs scenario()/selectedProject()/claude() helpers
candidates.fit_for_gap: C: implement VER-001 and VER-003 session bodies in place of stub()

evidence.claim: VER-001/VER-003 are stub() entries at sessions.mjs:314-316; VER-002 and POL-003 show the full scenario shape (scratch project, signed decision, session, observed tool calls, assertions)
kbd-phase-closure-adapter.mjs exports fixture/step/disposition/eventCounts for driving and observing canonical closure
IDR-002/IDR-003 (kbd-194-196-idr.mjs) already drive the real repair-and-resume operation directly; VER-001 can reuse it as the runner under value-scenario-verify

risks: Requires an operator-logged-in scratch Claude config; absent today (Gap E)
n=1 sample per scenario shows the behavior can happen, not that it is reliable
candidates.decision_rationale: All machinery exists; only the two scenario bodies are missing.

candidates.name: OpenCode 2.2.0 `opencode run --format json --standalone`
candidates.fit_for_gap: D/E: observe OpenCode as an additional installed surface under scratch isolation

evidence.claim: OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR is loaded after the global config and can override it; it does not replace or isolate it
Auth and session data live in ~/.local/share/opencode/ (auth.json); OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE disables reading ~/.claude prompt and skills

risks: Isolation needs scratch XDG_CONFIG_HOME/XDG_DATA_HOME; whether 2.2.0 honors XDG on macOS is UNVERIFIED and must be checked before any session
Without OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE=1 the run loads the operator's real ~/.claude skills, invalidating the surface under test
Event stream semantics of --format json are unverified for tool-call observation
candidates.decision_rationale: Usable only with explicit isolation; if XDG isolation cannot be confirmed, report OpenCode UNSUPPORTED/NOT_EXERCISED rather than run against real config.

candidates.name: dispatch-judge.sh with PROMETHEUS_KBD_JUDGE_* per-run override
candidates.fit_for_gap: G: cross-model review when models.toml judge and critic collide

evidence.claim: This phase's assess review ran with glm-5.3 via the override; gpt-5.5 via openai-proxy returned HTTP 400
dispatch-judge.sh:142-153 refuses when judge identity equals critic or producer identity, or no backup exists

risks: Findings are labelled unverified-producer-unknown until the producer identity is configured
The durable fix (distinct judge/critic or backup in models.toml) edits owner-owned config
candidates.decision_rationale: Works today with an honest label; the config fix is the owner's choice, not this phase's code.
